historical_context: The Ordnance QF 25-pounder was the standard British field gun in North Africa. Equipped the Royal Horse Artillery regiments supporting 7th Armoured Division. Highly effective in both field artillery and anti-tank roles. Two RHA regiments (3rd and 4th RHA) provided 64 guns total.

Ordnance QF 25-pounder Gun-Howitzer.notes: Versatile gun-howitzer. Effective in field artillery, counter-battery, and anti-tank roles.

special_rules: Effective Anti-Tank (AP round at close range)

strengths: Effective HE for infantry support and defensive fire
AP round can penetrate Panzer III and IV at close range
Proven in anti-tank role at Operation Battleaxe
weaknesses: Vulnerable when deployed - needs infantry protection
AP round less effective at long range
tactical_notes.typical_deployment: Support armored and motorized infantry attacks with HE fire. Provide defensive fire for leaguer positions. Emergency anti-tank defense with AP rounds. Counter-battery fire against German artillery. Use smoke to screen movements. RHA regiments were highly mobile and could keep pace with armored brigades.

HE.description: High explosive for infantry and soft targets

phase_6_data_source.organization: Each regiment has 2 batteries of 4 troops (4 guns per troop)
phase_6_data_source.notes: RHA = Royal Horse Artillery, elite mobile artillery

historical_engagements.operation_battleaxe: June 15-17, 1941. 25-pdrs inflicted heavy casualties on German tanks at Fort Capuzzo, destroying multiple Panzer III attacking British Matilda positions.
historical_engagements.effectiveness: Proved highly effective in anti-tank role when German armor attacked prepared positions.
